verses.zh: 耶稣又进了会堂，在那里有一个人枯干了一只手。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] entered the synagogue[NOTE:3] again, and a man was there who had a withered[NOTE:4] hand.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
See the note on synagogue in 1:21.
Withered means the man’s hand was shrunken and paralyzed.

verses.zh: 众人窥探耶稣，在安息日医治不医治，意思是要控告耶稣。
verses.en: They watched[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] closely to see if he would heal him on the Sabbath,[NOTE:3] so that they could accuse him.
notes: The term translated watched…closely is emotive, since it carries negative connotations. It means they were watching him out of the corner of their eye or spying on him.
Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The background for this is the view that only if life was endangered should one attempt to heal on the Sabbath (see the Mishnah, m. Shabbat 6.3; 12.1; 18.3; 19.2; m. Yoma 8.6).

verses.zh: 耶稣对那枯干一只手的人说：「起来，站在当中。」
verses.en: So he said to the man who had the withered hand, “Stand up among all these people.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “Stand up in the middle.”sn Most likely synagogues were arranged with benches along the walls and open space in the center for seating on the floor.

verses.zh: 又问众人说：「在安息日行善行恶，救命害命，哪样是可以的呢？」他们都不作声。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] he said to them, “Is it lawful to do good on the Sabbath, or evil, to save a life or destroy it?” But they were silent.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

verses.zh: 耶稣怒目周围看他们，忧愁他们的心刚硬，就对那人说：「伸出手来！」他把手一伸，手就复了原。
verses.en: After looking around[NOTE:1] at them in anger, grieved by the hardness of their hearts,[NOTE:2] he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.[NOTE:3]
notes: The aorist participle περιβλεψάμενος (periblepsamenos) has been translated as antecedent (prior) to the action of the main verb. It could also be translated as contemporaneous (“Looking around…he said”).
This term is a collective singular in the Greek text.

The passive was restored points to healing by God. Now the question became: Would God exercise his power through Jesus, if what Jesus was doing were wrong? Note also Jesus’ “labor.” He simply spoke and it was so.

verses.zh: 法利赛人出去，同希律一党的人商议怎样可以除灭耶稣。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] the Pharisees[NOTE:2] went out immediately and began plotting with the Herodians,[NOTE:3] as to how they could assassinate[NOTE:4] him.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of previous action(s) in the narrative.
See the note on Pharisees in 2:16.

Grk inserts “against him” after “Herodians.” This is somewhat redundant in English and has not been translated.sn The Herodians are mentioned in the NT only once in Matt (22:16 = Mark 12:13) and twice in Mark (3:6; 12:13; some mss also read “Herodians” instead of “Herod” in Mark 8:15). It is generally assumed that as a group the Herodians were Jewish supporters of the Herodian dynasty (or of Herod Antipas in particular). In every instance they are linked with the Pharisees. This probably reflects agreement regarding political objectives (nationalism as opposed to submission to the yoke of Roman oppression) rather than philosophy or religious beliefs.
Grk “destroy.”

verses.zh: 耶稣和门徒退到海边去，有许多人从加利利跟随他。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus went away with his disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed him.[NOTE:2] And from Judea,
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
The word “him” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context.

verses.zh: 还有许多人听见他所做的大事，就从犹太、耶路撒冷、以土买、约旦河外，并泰尔、西顿的四方来到他那里。
verses.en: Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] Idumea, beyond the Jordan River,[NOTE:2] and around Tyre[NOTE:3] and Sidon[NOTE:4] a great multitude came to him when they heard about the things he had done.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
“River” is not in the Greek text but is supplied for clarity. The region referred to here is sometimes known as Transjordan (i.e., “across the Jordan”).
For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

These last two locations, Tyre and Sidon, represented an expansion outside of traditional Jewish territory. Jesus’ reputation continued to expand into new regions.map For location see Map1-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

verses.zh: 他因为人多，就吩咐门徒叫一只小船伺候着，免得众人拥挤他。
verses.en: Because of the crowd, he told his disciples to have a small boat[NOTE:1] ready for him so the crowd[NOTE:2] would not press toward him.
notes: See the note at Mark 1:19 for a description of the first-century fishing boat discovered in 1986 near Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.
Grk “they”; the referent (the crowd) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他治好了许多人，所以凡有灾病的，都挤进来要摸他。
verses.en: For he had healed many, so that all who were afflicted with diseases pressed toward him in order to touch him.

verses.zh: 污鬼无论何时看见他，就俯伏在他面前，喊着说：「你是　神的儿子。」
verses.en: And whenever the unclean spirits[NOTE:1] saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, “You are the Son of God.”
notes: Unclean spirits refers to evil spirits.

verses.zh: 耶稣再三地嘱咐他们，不要把他显露出来。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] he sternly ordered them not to make him known.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.

Jesus did not permit the demons to make him known because the time for such disclosure was not yet at hand, and such a revelation would have certainly been misunderstood by the people. In all likelihood, if the people had understood him early on to be the Son of God, or Messiah, they would have reduced his mission to one of political deliverance from Roman oppression (cf. John 6:15). Jesus wanted to avoid, as much as possible, any premature misunderstanding about who he was and what he was doing. However, at the end of his ministry, he did not deny such a title when the high priest asked him (14:61-62).

verses.zh: 耶稣上了山，随自己的意思叫人来；他们便来到他那里。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] Jesus went up the mountain[NOTE:2] and called for those he wanted, and they came to him.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.

Or “up a mountain” (εἰς τὸ ὅρος, eis to horos).sn The expression up the mountain here may be idiomatic or generic, much like the English “he went to the hospital” (cf. 15:29), or even intentionally reminiscent of Exod 24:12 (LXX), since the genre of the Sermon on the Mount seems to be that of a new Moses giving a new law.

verses.zh: 他就设立十二个人，要他们常和自己同在，也要差他们去传道，
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] appointed 12[NOTE:2] so that they would be with him and he could send them to preach
notes: Grk “And he.”

The phrase “whom he named apostles” is lacking in the majority of mss (A C2 D L ƒ1 33 565 579 1241 1424 M latt sy; SBL). Several primary Alexandrian and other key witnesses (א B C* W Δ Θ ƒ13 28 co) include the phrase, rendering the external evidence strongly in favor of this reading. It is possible that the Alexandrian witnesses have inserted these words to bring the text in line with Luke 6:13 (TCGNT 69), but against this is the internal evidence of Mark’s style: Mark tends toward gratuitous redundancy. However, significant Western and Byzantine mss along with other authorities lack the clause, which is against the Byzantine tendencies. The key issue, however, is that both the wording of the clause and its location in the verse varies significantly among the witnesses, which suggests that it was indeed borrowed from the Lukan parallel. The NA28 puts the words in brackets indicating doubts about their authenticity.

verses.zh: 并给他们权柄赶鬼。
verses.en: and to have authority to cast out demons.

verses.zh: 这十二个人有西门（耶稣又给他起名叫彼得），
verses.en: [NOTE:1] To Simon[NOTE:2] he gave the name Peter;
notes: The phrase “he appointed 12” at the beginning of v. 16 is lacking in the majority of mss (A C2 D L Θ ƒ1 33 700 1241 1424 M lat sy bo), including several key witnesses. Some significant authorities include the phrase (א B C* Δ 565 579 pc). The omission may have been caused by haplography in combination with homoioarcton: The first word of the clause in question is καί (kai), and the first word after the clause in question is also καί. And the first two letters of the second word, in each instance, are επ (ep). Early scribes may have jumped accidentally from the first καί to the second, omitting the intervening material. Metzger suggests that “the clause seems to be needed in order to pick up the thread of ver. 14 after the parenthesis ἵνα…δαιμόνια” (TCGNT 69). This seems to be a stretch. Further, the external evidence in favor of the words is not as compelling as it could be (the addition of “whom he named apostles” in 3:14 actually has stronger evidence, yet we considered it spurious). A decision is difficult but the shorter reading is preferred. NA28 puts the words in brackets.

In the various lists of the 12, Simon (that is, Peter) is always mentioned first (see also Matt 10:1-4; Luke 6:13-16; Acts 1:13) and the first four are always the same, though not in the same order after Peter.

verses.zh: 还有西庇太的儿子雅各和雅各的兄弟约翰（又给这两个人起名叫半尼其，就是雷子的意思），
verses.en: to James and his brother John, the sons of Zebedee,[NOTE:1] he gave the name Boanerges (that is, “sons of thunder”);
notes: Grk “to James, the son of Zebedee, and John, the brother of James.”

verses.zh: 又有安得烈、腓力、巴多罗买、马太、多马、亚勒腓的儿子雅各、和达太，并奋锐党的西门，
verses.en: and Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew,[NOTE:1] Matthew, Thomas,[NOTE:2] James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus,[NOTE:3] Simon the Zealot,[NOTE:4]
notes: Bartholomew (meaning “son of Tolmai” in Aramaic) could be another name for Nathanael mentioned in John 1:45.
This is the “doubting Thomas” of John 20:24-29.
This disciple is called Λεββαῖον (Lebbaion, “Lebbaeus”) in D it; see the discussion of the parallel text in Matt 10:3 where conflation occurs among other witnesses as well.

Grk “the Cananean,” but according to both BDAG 507 s.v. Καναναῖος and L&N 11.88, this term has no relation at all to the geographical terms for Cana or Canaan, but is derived from the Aramaic term for “enthusiast, zealot” (see Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13), possibly because of an earlier affiliation with the party of the Zealots. He may not have been technically a member of the particular Jewish nationalistic party known as “Zealots” (since according to some scholars this party had not been organized at that time), but simply someone who was zealous for Jewish independence from Rome, in which case the term would refer to his temperament.

verses.zh: 还有卖耶稣的加略人犹大。
verses.en: and Judas Iscariot,[NOTE:1] who betrayed him.[NOTE:2]
notes: There is some debate about what the name Iscariot means. It probably alludes to a region in Judea and thus might make Judas the only non-Galilean in the group. Several explanations for the name Iscariot have been proposed, but it is probably transliterated Hebrew with the meaning “man of Kerioth” (there are at least two villages that had that name). For further discussion see D. L. Bock, Luke (BECNT), 1:546; also D. A. Carson, John, 304.
Grk “who even betrayed him.”

verses.zh: 耶稣进了一个屋子，众人又聚集，甚至他连饭也顾不得吃。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] Jesus[NOTE:2] went home, and a crowd gathered so that they were not able to eat.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.
Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶稣的亲属听见，就出来要拉住他，因为他们说他癫狂了。
verses.en: When his family[NOTE:1] heard this they went out to restrain him, for they said, “He is out of his mind.”
notes: On the meaning “family” for οἱ παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ (hoi par’ autou), see BDAG 756-57 s.v. παρά A.3.b.β.ב.sn The incident involving the religious leaders accusing Jesus of being in league with the devil (3:22-30) is sandwiched between Mark’s mention of Jesus’ family coming to restrain him (the Greek word for restrain here is also used to mean arrest; see Mark 6:17; 12:12; 14:1, 44, 46, 49, 51) because they thought he was out of his mind (3:21). It is probably Mark’s intention in this structure to show that Jesus’ family is to be regarded as not altogether unlike the experts in the law [scribes] in their perception of the true identity of Jesus; they are incorrect in their understanding of him as well. The tone is obviously one of sadness and the emphasis on Jesus’ true family in vv. 31-35 serves to underscore the comparison between his relatives and the scribes on the one hand, and those who truly obey God on the other. tc Western witnesses D W it, instead of reading οἱ παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ (hoi par’ autou, here translated “family”), have περὶ αὐτοῦ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ λοιποί (peri autou hoi grammateis kai hoi loipoi, “[when] the scribes and others [heard] about him”). But this reading is obviously motivated, for it removes the embarrassing statement about Jesus’ family’s opinion of him as “out of his mind” and transfers this view to the Lord’s opponents. The fact that virtually all other witnesses have οἱ παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ here, coupled with the strong internal evidence for the shorter reading, shows this Western reading to be secondary.

gr.gloss: He is out of His mind

verses.zh: 从耶路撒冷下来的文士说：「他是被别西卜附着」；又说：「他是靠着鬼王赶鬼。」
verses.en: The experts in the law[NOTE:1] who came down from Jerusalem[NOTE:2] said, “He is possessed by Beelzebul,”[NOTE:3] and, “By the ruler[NOTE:4] of demons he casts out demons!”
notes: Or “The scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 1:22.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Grk “He has Beelzebul.”sn Beelzebul is another name for Satan. So some people, particularly here the experts in the law, recognized Jesus’ work as supernatural, but called it diabolical.
Or “prince.”

verses.zh: 耶稣叫他们来，用比喻对他们说：「撒但怎能赶出撒但呢？
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] he called them and spoke to them in parables:[NOTE:2] “How can Satan cast out Satan?
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of previous action(s) in the narrative.

Jesus spoke two parables to demonstrate the absurdity of the thinking of the religious leaders who maintained that he was in league with Satan and that he actually derived his power from the devil. The first parable (vv. 23-26) teaches that if Jesus cast out demons by the ruler of the demons, then in reality Satan is fighting against himself, with the result that his kingdom has come to an end. The second parable (v. 27) about tying up a strong man proves that Jesus does not need to align himself with the devil because Jesus is more powerful. Jesus defeated Satan at his temptation (1:12-13) and by his exorcisms he clearly demonstrated himself to be stronger than the devil. The passage reveals the desperate condition of the religious leaders, who in their hatred for Jesus end up attributing the work of the Holy Spirit to Satan (a position for which they will be held accountable, 3:29-30). For an explanation of what a parable is, see the note on parables in 4:2.

verses.zh: 若一国自相纷争，那国就站立不住；
verses.en: If[NOTE:1] a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom will not be able to stand.
notes: The three conditional statements in vv. 24-26 express the logical result of the assumption that Jesus heals by Satan’s power, expressed by the religious leaders. The point is clear: If the leaders are correct, then Satan’s kingdom will not stand, so the suggestion makes no sense. Satan would not seek to heal.

verses.zh: 若一家自相纷争，那家就站立不住。
verses.en: If a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.

verses.zh: 若撒但自相攻打纷争，他就站立不住，必要灭亡。
verses.en: And if Satan rises against himself and is divided, he is not able to stand and his end has come.

verses.zh: 没有人能进壮士家里，抢夺他的家具；必先捆住那壮士，才可以抢夺他的家。
verses.en: But no one is able to enter a strong man’s[NOTE:1] house and steal his property unless he first ties up the strong man. Then he can thoroughly plunder his house.[NOTE:2]
notes: The strong man here pictures Satan.

Some see the imagery here as similar to Eph 4:7-10, although no opponents are explicitly named in that passage. Jesus has the victory over Satan. Jesus’ acts of healing mean that the war is being won and the kingdom is coming.

verses.zh: 我实在告诉你们，世人一切的罪和一切亵渎的话都可得赦免；
verses.en: I tell you the truth,[NOTE:1] people will be forgiven for all sins, even all the blasphemies they utter.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “Truly (ἀμήν, amēn), I say to you.”
Grk “all the sins and blasphemies they may speak will be forgiven the sons of men.”

verses.zh: 凡亵渎圣灵的，却永不得赦免，乃要担当永远的罪。」
verses.en: But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven, but is guilty of an eternal sin”[NOTE:1]
notes: Is guilty of an eternal sin. This passage has troubled many people, who have wondered whether or not they have committed this eternal sin. Three things must be kept in mind: (1) the nature of the sin is to ascribe what is the obvious work of the Holy Spirit (e.g., releasing people from Satan’s power) to Satan himself; (2) it is not simply a momentary doubt or sinful attitude, but is indeed a settled condition which opposes the Spirit’s work, as typified by the religious leaders who opposed Jesus; and (3) a person who is concerned about it has probably never committed this sin, for those who commit it here (i.e., the religious leaders) are not in the least concerned about Jesus’ warning. On this last point see W. W. Wessel, “Mark,” EBC 8:645-46.

verses.zh: 这话是因为他们说：「他是被污鬼附着的。」
verses.en: (because they said, “He has an unclean spirit”[NOTE:1]).
notes: Unclean spirit refers to an evil spirit.

verses.zh: 当下，耶稣的母亲和弟兄来，站在外边，打发人去叫他。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus’[NOTE:2] mother and his brothers[NOTE:3] came. Standing[NOTE:4] outside, they sent word to him, to summon him.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Grk “his”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The issue of whether Jesus had brothers (siblings) has had a long history in the church. Epiphanius, in the 4th century, argued that Mary was a perpetual virgin and had no offspring other than Jesus. Others argued that these brothers were really cousins. Nothing in the text suggests any of this. See also John 7:3.
Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.

verses.zh: 有许多人在耶稣周围坐着，他们就告诉他说：「看哪，你母亲和你弟兄在外边找你。」
verses.en: A crowd was sitting around him and they said to him, “Look, your mother and your brothers[NOTE:1] are outside looking for you.”
notes: ‡ Many mss read “and your sisters” here after “your brothers” (A D Γ 700 pm it). However, the pedigree of several of the mss which lack this phrase is considerable (א B C K L W Δ Θ ƒ1,13 28 33 565 892 1241 1424 2542 pm lat sy). It seems likely that this phrase was added by an early Western scribe to harmonize this statement with Jesus’ response in v. 35. NA27 has the words in brackets, indicating some doubt as to their authenticity.

verses.zh: 耶稣回答说：「谁是我的母亲？谁是我的弟兄？」
verses.en: He answered them and said, “Who are my mother and my brothers?”[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “Who is my mother and my brothers?” The use of the singular verb ἐστιν (estin) here singles out Mary above Jesus’ brothers, giving her special prominence (see ExSyn 401-2). This is slightly unnatural in English since the predicate nominative is plural, though, so a plural verb was used in the translation.

verses.zh: 就四面观看那周围坐着的人，说：「看哪，我的母亲，我的弟兄。
verses.en: And looking at those who were sitting around him in a circle, he said, “Here[NOTE:1] are my mother and my brothers!
notes: Grk “Behold my mother and my brothers.”

verses.zh: 凡遵行　神旨意的人就是我的弟兄姊妹和母亲了。」
verses.en: For whoever does the will of God is[NOTE:1] my brother and sister and mother.”
notes: The pleonastic pronoun οὗτος (houtos, “this one”) which precedes this verb has not been translated.
